A new survey reveals most people prefer human elders over AI for genuine life advice.
Evidence: Maltesers poll, 2,000 adults, AI limits
#Culture #Technology

Over 70% of Brits believe AI chatbots can never replace the authentic wisdom, lived experience, and emotional connection offered by human elders.
Stated Judgement: (+1.00, +1.00) — Redemption

While human connection remains vital, the poll was commissioned by Maltesers for a 90th anniversary marketing campaign featuring a playful ad panel.
Resulting Judgement: (+1.00, +1.00) — Conditional

Verdict: PASS — The Path of Redemption. Genuine human insights are celebrated through a clever commercial campaign that highlights real social bonds.

Integrity: Conditionally Sound (Hypocrisy: 1.4, Uncertainty z: 0)

- Public Sentiment: PASS (+0.8, +0.5) — Valid preference for human elders.
- Corporate Sponsor: COND (+0.4, +0.2) — Commercial PR framing.
A survey of 2,000 adults commissioned by confectionery brand Maltesers found widespread preference for human wisdom over AI chatbots for personal advice.

The Bright Side:
Commercial marketing successfully champions the irreplaceable warmth of intergenerational connection over cold digital automation.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Treating a brand promotional poll as a purely academic sociological study misattributes commercial entertainment as deep data.

Social Physics Analysis:
Brand marketing merges corporate self-interest with genuine cultural appreciation for elders, running a mild promotional loop atop real social truths.

The Trajectory: The Path of Redemption.
When commercial PR aligns with authentic human values, it plots a stable trajectory toward Redemption through shared cultural resonance.

The Unavoidable Truth: Lived human experience provides empathy and context that algorithms cannot replicate.

The Unavoidable Lie: Confectionery brand surveys are neutral sociological studies.

Honoring ancestral wisdom preserves the irreplaceable fabric of human community.

The post AI Chatbots Will Never Replace Advice From Elders, Say Seven of 10 in New Poll appeared first on Good News Network.

Actual Article Body:
More than seven in 10 Brits believe AI will never replace advice from their elders.

A study of 2,000 adults found while 21 percent use these artificial intelligence tools for help several times a week, 92 percent believe some forms of wisdom can only be gained through lived experience.

In fact, 71 percent feel AI advice will never replace genuine human connection, with mums (39 percent), female friends (20 percent) and sisters (12 percent) ranked among the most trusted sources of advice.

It also emerged those polled go to older people for tips on how to make a relationship last (19 percent), coping with stress (19 percent) and navigate a career change (13 percent).

Older generations are also valued for their practical know-how, including weeding the garden (16 percent), bleeding a radiator (18 percent) and removing stains from clothes (25 percent).

The research was commissioned by Maltesers, the candy company, which is encouraging people to submit their questions to its ‘Age Intelligence panel’, a playful spoof on AI hosted by British actor Sue Johnston—as part of the malted milk ball confection’s 90th anniversary.

“AI is very handy for quick answers,” said the actress. ”But it can’t tell you what a real person would say, remind you to take a cardigan sweater, or confirm that you’re definitely not overreacting (when you probably are).”

“Real wisdom comes from living through life’s ups and downs – and from the people who’ve been there with you, armed with a story, an opinion and a cup of tea they insist you have before making any decisions.

The research also found 55 percent of those who believed that AI will never replace advice from older generations say it’s because they offer real-life experience that technology simply cannot replicate.

Almost half believe advice from older people is more authentic, with 43 percent believing they’re better able to understand the nuances and emotions behind a situation.

Additionally, respondents value the personal stories and life lessons they provide, according to the OnePoll findings.

Among the most valued pearls of wisdom cited by those surveyed were “save for a rainy day” and “treat others as you would like to be treated”, as well as “life is too short to hold grudges”.

However, 64 percent of AI users admitted they have sought help from a chatbot when they could have, instead, spoken to a real person.

Like many of us would, 4 in 10 chose AI because it provided immediate answers. 25% appreciated the anonymity they felt, and another quarter preferred AI because it can sometimes explain things more simply.

Despite this, trust remains a challenge when it comes to personal topics— with just 18% relying on AI-generated parenting advice and 17% for relationship advice.

By comparison, 77% prefer advice from real people on personal topics.

Claire Norgate from Maltesers, which is also celebrating its long-standing partnership with Comic Relief which has raised more than £8.5 million for charity.

“There are some things it simply can’t replicate—the stories, perspective, humor and connection that come from real-life experience.

Whether it’s a parent, sibling, friend, or someone from an older generation, sometimes the best advice comes from simply having a conversation.
